title: Hedge Funds: Strategies, Survivorship and Other Biases, and Madoff

maps.specifics: Reported: 'survivorship bias questions'. The bias sibling set (survivorship, selection/self-selection, backfill, reporting) is the discrimination GARP tests. Madoff (Reading 96) is rated Very Important and functions as the red-flags case study; treat it as a case-lesson matching item against the other case studies.

selectors.name: Hedge fund strategies and their mechanics
selectors.what: Identify, compare or describe the mechanics, legs, returns and risks of equity long/short, dedicated short, nonhedged equity, global macro, fixed-income and convertible arbitrage, relative value, event-driven and merger arbitrage, and distressed securities. Includes the numerical illustrations: share-for-share merger arbitrage profit at close (offer ratio x acquirer price - target price per target share) and the distressed capital-structure trade (bond gain plus coupons and recovery, plus the short on the junior security).
selectors.theory: Convertible arbitrage is long the convertible and short the stock, delta hedged, earning coupon, short interest and monetised volatility. Merger arbitrage is long the target and, in a share-for-share deal, short the acquirer at the exchange ratio, earning the spread, with failed-deal losses that can far exceed the gains. Distressed trades go long senior and short junior, and the core risk is a restructuring that takes longer than expected. Global macro trades more liquid instruments than the other strategies.

selectors.name: Hedge fund risks, systemic risk, regulation, structure
selectors.what: Risks faced by hedge fund investors (portfolio-level and investment-level, and the five incremental risks), the channels by which hedge funds raise systemic risk (LTCM, Amaranth, Archegos), regulatory approaches (Dodd-Frank, AIFMD, other jurisdictions) and the typical structure (general and limited partners, master-feeder, domicile, 2 and 20 taxation). Includes the leverage spiral: sale needed to restore a target debt-to-equity ratio, s = L - k x E', where E' = V' - L.
selectors.theory: With 75 of debt on stock worth 100, leverage is 3x; after a 10% fall the stock is worth 90, equity 15 and leverage 5x, so selling 30 (75 - 3 x 15) restores 3x, and forced sales feed contagion. Systemic risk runs through fire-sale unwinding of a failed strategy and through losses imposed on lenders and counterparties. Overly strict regulation reduces the liquidity that hedge funds supply as investors of last resort.

selectors.name: Survivorship bias against its sibling biases
selectors.what: Tell survivorship bias from selection (sample selection), reporting, backfill and infrequent-sampling biases: which bias a described data problem is, and the direction of its effect on reported returns, alpha, beta and volatility.

selectors.name: Madoff red flags matched to other cases
selectors.what: A case-to-lesson matching item: which red flag or lesson belongs to Madoff (in-house custody and execution, a tiny unknown auditor, secrecy, family in key roles, no negative months, split-strike claims that did not reconcile with options volume) rather than to LTCM, Archegos or the failed prime brokers (Lehman, MF Global, Refco).

selectors.name: Manager evaluation themes and questions
selectors.what: Themes and questions an investor weighs when evaluating a hedge fund manager: strategy and edge, concentration, gross and net exposure, stop losses, use of shorts and derivatives, capacity, equity ownership of the team, and a track record that is comparable, audited, long enough and produced by the team still in place, plus background and reference checks.

selectors.name: Operational due diligence on a fund
selectors.what: How due diligence is performed on a hedge fund's operational environment: internal controls and compliance, counterparty diversification, consistency of documents (OM, LPA, Form ADV), an unqualified audit opinion, and red flags such as incentive fees in loss years or general partner withdrawals.
